newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says war games in S.Korea threaten talks.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says war games in S.Korea threaten talks.

text.p: North Korea blasted the United States and South Korea on Thursday for planning to hold joint military drills while conducting preliminary talks aimed at drafting a peace accord for the Korean Peninsula.

Radio Pyongyang quoted a North Korean spokesman from the Committee for the Peaceful Reunification of the Fatherland as saying that the drills were "an extremely threatening act". according to reports monitored by the Tokyo-based news agency Radiopress.

"They (the U.S. and South Korea) are talking peace but if they are going to act against the process with these war drills, then there is no reason for communication and the talks have no meaning," the spokesman said.
"We can prepare to face the talks and we can prepare to face war," he said.

Officials from North and South Korea, China and the United States held a limited round of talks in New York on Tuesday aimed at setting a date and other specifics for more substantial discussions on securing a peace accord to replace the armistice that ended the Korean War.
The four sides, all parties to the armistice agreement, agreed on Wednesday to hold another round of preparatory talks.
The North Korean spokesman said the joint exercises, known as "Ulchi Focus Lens", should be suspended because the North was "irritated by the danger of the military drills", Radiopress reported.
The U.S.-South Korean joint military exercise is scheduled for August 18 to 29 and involves 16,500 U.S. military personnel and tens of thousands South Koreans.
The joint drills have been conducted every year since 1976.
